children: H. Lundbeck A/S said the last patient has been randomized in DEEp SEA, a global Phase III trial of bexicaserin for seizures in Dravet syndrome; over 100 participants enrolled, with an option to enter a 52-week open-label extension.

Last patient randomized in DEEp SEA
Signals enrollment completion; timelines to top-line data and regulatory path firm up.
Phase III Dravet trial; >100 enrolled
Pivotal scale in a rare, high-need indication; potential future revenue stream.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
Robust design boosts credibility of potential efficacy/safety signals.
Option for 52-week OLE
Supports longer-term safety exposure needed for filings and label.
Bexicaserin has FDA BTD for DEEs
Could expedite development/review if efficacy shown, improving NPV.
Second Phase III (DEEp OCEAN) enrolled
Broader program progress de-risks platform across DEEs beyond Dravet.
Context by AI Analyst

This is a mid-cycle R&D milestone that moves bexicaserin closer to pivotal readout but provides no efficacy data yet. A clear, positive top-line result from DEEp SEA (and DEEp OCEAN) and regulatory dialogue would turn this into a larger catalyst.
